subject: Acme Cloud: request for service recourse after sustained latency regression
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acmecloud.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@acmecloud.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency spike — impact to inference calls and next steps

Irene,

Over the last 36 hours we've observed a sustained increase in p50/p95 serving latency for the dedicated pool backing our inference endpoints. p50 has moved from ~40ms to ~350ms and p95 is consistently >1.2s. This is affecting our 3rd-party integrations and a customer-facing feature — we're seeing a measurable uptick in errors and timeouts.

We've pulled traces and a subset of logs and attached them here for your ops team (support_log_20261020.zip). Per our contract (SLA §3.1), this looks like a sustained latency regression beyond the allowed threshold. We need:
- A clear root-cause summary by EOD tomorrow (Oct 21)
- Proposed remediation and timeline
- Proposed service recourse (credits / free months) while we evaluate impact and consider our renewal on Nov 30

Please confirm receipt and next steps.

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Cloud
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 14:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — impact to inference calls and next steps

Elena —

Thanks for the heads up and for attaching the logs. We’ve opened an incident with our SRE team and Jonas is on rotation to triage immediately. Apologies for the disruption — we take P50/P95 regressions very seriously.

Immediate next steps:
- Jonas to post a preliminary RCA timeline (target: 24 hours)
- I’ll coordinate a shared timeline and any interim mitigations (routing to a hot spare model pool, temporarily increasing capacity)
- Karthik and Lauren are looped to start internal approval flow for any goodwill compensation we offer while we investigate

We’ll aim to have an actionable update by Oct 21 COB PST.

Irene Choi
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Elena Torres <elena.torres@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — preliminary findings

Elena / team —

Preliminary findings (quick summary):
- Root cause: a misconfiguration in autoscale policy combined with an anomalous request pattern from a third-party client caused persistent queueing on the model servers between Oct 19 22:00 UTC and Oct 20 08:00 UTC.
- What we saw: sustained CPU/GPU queue depth increases and degraded KV cache hit-rate leading to higher token generation latency (p50 rose to ~300–400ms).
- Remediation already applied: adjusted autoscale thresholds, killed a problematic worker pool, and pushed a minor scheduling fix. Observed return to baseline for p50 after the fix on Oct 21 03:40 UTC.

Attachments: I’ve uploaded the short incident timeline and the log slice used (support_log_20261020.zip referenced).

Proposal for makegood while we negotiate:
- Option A (customer-friendly): One month of Dedicated capacity credit (applies to Nov 2026 invoice) + one-time invoice credit of $15,000 to offset observed downstream impact.
- Option B (conservative): 10% invoice credit for Oct + a tech support package for 90 days (no billing credit).

Rationale: Option A is higher short-term cost but increases retention likelihood ahead of their renewal; Option B limits financial exposure.

Happy to jump on a call to walk through the timeline.

— Jonas
Head of SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — finance perspective and suggested terms

Team —

From a finance/control perspective I have two suggestions to keep exposure reasonable while addressing Acme’s impact:
1) Cap the one-time credit to $12,500 if we go with Option A (this aligns with previous concessions and legal wants a $12.5k ceiling for discretionary credits).
2) If Acme wants a free month, it should apply only to the Dedicated pool (not to additional services) and require a written amendment signed by procurement.

I’ve drafted a short proposed_terms document (proposed_makegood_terms.pdf) that captures: scope of credit, effective dates, non-precedential language, and acceptance flow (Procurement signs DocuSign link). I’ll attach it to this thread for Irene to share.

— Lauren
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Request for executive sign-off: proposed Acme makegood

Marissa —

Acme Cloud experienced a sustained latency regression that impacted production between Oct 19–20. Jonas completed remediation and has restored baseline performance. Acme has signaled commercial concern and is asking for remediation credits ahead of renewal.

Recommended package (internal ask):
- One month Dedicated pool credit applied to Nov 2026 invoice (non-transferable)
- One-time invoice credit of $12,500
- Terms as drafted in proposed_makegood_terms.pdf; acceptance via DocuSign (link below)

Why approve: this is a strategic account — potential churn risk at renewal if we don’t show a strong remediation posture. The total exposure (~$12.5k + value of one month of dedicated capacity) is within discretionary limits for a one-off goodwill gesture. Legal/Revenue Ops have added non-precedential language.

Please reply with APPROVE / DENY / COUNTER and any conditions. Elena and Procurement are looped.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request for executive sign-off: proposed Acme makegood

APPROVE with edits —

Approve the one-month Dedicated credit and a one-time invoice credit of $12,500. Conditions:
- This is one-off, documented as non-precedential in the amendment
- Procurement must sign the amendment before any credit is applied (DocuSign link)
- Add a technical post-mortem meeting between Acme and our SRE leaders (Jonas to present) within 10 business days

Lauren/legal: please convert proposed_makegood_terms.pdf into an amendment and route for signature. Irene: please coordinate acceptance with Elena and Procurement; confirm acceptance here when signed.

— Marissa Cole
SVP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acmecloud.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@acmecloud.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Oct 2026 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme Cloud: request for service recourse after sustained latency regression

Irene / team —

Thank you for the quick response and the remediation work. We’re OK to proceed with the one-month Dedicated credit + $12.5k invoice credit as outlined, pending the amendment. Procurement is ready to review the DocuSign and will push back if they need changes, but overall this should be acceptable.

Please send the amendment link and confirm when the credit has been applied. We’ll schedule the post-mortem on our side once Jonas proposes times.

Elena
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Cloud
